advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Require the `${var:?}` guard to appear before (and dominate) the deletion line for each targeted variable, not merely anywhere in the file.
evidence: scripts/check_destructive_test_exec.py:72-74 `_guarded_vars` regex-scans the entire `script_text` with no position tracking
scripts/check_destructive_test_exec.py:92 `if all(n in guarded for n in names): continue` uses the global set regardless of where the guard sits relative to the rm
Docstring line 19-20 promises the guard is 'for the same variable the deletion targets' — the implementation does not verify the guard precedes/dominates the deletion
advisory.finding: `_guarded_vars` collects `${var:?}` guards from anywhere in the script and clears a deletion if all its interpolated names appear in that global set, with no ordering/reachability check. A `: "${dir:?}"` written AFTER the `rm -rf "${dir}"/*`, or inside an unreachable/else branch, still clears the deletion — contradicting the docstring's 'for the same variable the deletion targets' and letting an ineffective guard pass the gate.
scenarios: Script: `rm -rf "${dir}"/*` on line 3, then `: "${dir:?}"` on line 5 — deletion already happened but the gate reports clean

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Scope the seam check to the command that actually performs the matched deletion rather than any occurrence on the physical line.
evidence: scripts/check_destructive_test_exec.py:83 only skips lines whose lstrip startswith '#'
scripts/check_destructive_test_exec.py:87 `if _SEAM_RE.search(line): continue` tests the whole line, not the deletion target/command actually invoked
A line `rm -rf "${dir}"/* ; echo "${RM_CMD:-rm}"` would be cleared despite the raw rm
advisory.finding: Comment stripping and seam detection are line-based and coarse: `stripped.startswith("#")` only skips whole-line comments (a trailing `rm -rf "${dir}"/*  # note` is still scanned, which is fine, but the inverse—`_SEAM_RE.search(line)` matching a seam token elsewhere on a line that also contains a raw `rm`—clears a genuine unguarded deletion on that same physical line).
scenarios: A single line containing both a raw destructive rm and an unrelated `${X_CMD:-rm}` token

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add fixtures asserting the gate flags alternate rm flag spellings/orders (rm -fr, rm -r -f, rm -f -r, rm -Rf).
evidence: scripts/check_destructive_test_exec.py:46-48 `_RM_RE = re.compile(r"\brm\s+(?:-[a-zA-Z]*(?:rf|fr)[a-zA-Z]*|(?:-[rR]\s+-f|-f\s+-[rR]))\S*\s+([^\n;&|]*)")` deliberately handles -fr / -r -f / -f -r / -R orderings
VULNERABLE / SEAMED / GUARDED / SET_U_ONLY fixtures all use `rm -rf` only — no fixture exercises `rm -fr`, `rm -r -f`, `rm -f -r`, or `rm -Rf`
Named violating input: a test that execs a script containing `rm -fr "${dir}"/*` (an unguarded deletion the gate must catch) is never asserted
scripts/check_destructive_test_exec.py:108-115 requires `isinstance(node.func.value, ast.Name) and node.func.value.id == "subprocess"` — only the dotted attribute form is matched
TEST_EXEC fixture uses only `subprocess.run(['sh', 'purge.sh'], check=False)`; no fixture uses a bound-name import form

Named violating input: a test file `from subprocess import run\ndef test_it():\n    run(['sh','purge.sh'])` executing the VULNERABLE script is not asserted (would go unflagged, and no test documents this as intended-or-not)
advisory.finding: The alternate rm flag spellings the regex was written to catch (rm -fr, rm -r -f, rm -f -r, and the -R spelling) have no test — every fixture uses only 'rm -rf'. A regression narrowing _RM_RE to only -rf would pass the whole suite while silently missing 'rm -fr "${dir}"/*'.
merged_from: _is_exec_call only recognizes the attribute form subprocess.run(...); a test invoking exec via 'from subprocess import run; run([...])' is a silent false negative, and no test pins this boundary of the detector.
scenarios: A refactor simplifying _RM_RE to only match '-rf' leaves the added flag-order alternatives untested and would ship a detection hole
advisory.suggested_fix: Add a table-driven test parametrizing the deletion prefix over ['rm -rf','rm -fr','rm -r -f','rm -f -r','rm -Rf'] against the unguarded target, asserting each is flagged.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a fixture with a multi-variable deletion target where only one variable is ${var:?}-guarded, asserting it is still flagged.
evidence: scripts/check_destructive_test_exec.py:92 `if all(n in guarded for n in names): continue` — the 'all' quantifier only matters when a target has multiple interpolated names
GUARDED fixture has a single variable `dir`; no fixture uses a target like `"${a}"/"${b}"` where only `${a:?}` is guarded
Named violating input: a script deleting `rm -rf "${a}"/"${b}"/*` with only `: "${a:?}"` present should still be flagged (b is unguarded) — untested
advisory.finding: The multi-variable partial-guard branch `all(n in guarded for n in names)` is untested: no fixture has a deletion target containing two variables where only one carries a ${var:?} guard.
scenarios: A refactor changing `all` to `any` would pass every existing test while wrongly clearing a partially-guarded multi-variable target

blocking.checklist_item: - [ ] Detect `subprocess`-exec calls via `from subprocess import run` and aliased/wrapper forms, not only `subprocess.<func>` on a Name base.
evidence: scripts/check_destructive_test_exec.py:108-115 `_is_exec_call` requires `isinstance(node.func.value, ast.Name) and node.func.value.id == "subprocess"`
`search_files` for `from subprocess import` returns no matches today, but nothing prevents a future test from using that idiom, which the gate would not flag
The gate's negative verdict when this idiom is used cannot be distinguished from a genuine clean result (fail-open check)
scripts/check_destructive_test_exec.py:102-104 requires `isinstance(sub.value, str)` and `sub.value.endswith(".sh")`
scripts/check_destructive_test_exec.py:128-130 resolves `root / literal` and silently `continue`s when not a file
A test that computes the script path (very common with tmp_path fixtures) produces no Constant matching `.sh`, so `_script_literals` returns [] and no finding is emitted
blocking.finding: Exec detection only matches attribute calls whose base Name is literally `subprocess` (`subprocess.run(...)`). A test using `from subprocess import run` (or an aliased import / a thin wrapper helper) that execs the same destructive script is silently not scanned, so the gate passes while the hazard is present — its miss path is indistinguishable from 'no violation'.
merged_from: Only `.sh` string-literal arguments in the exec call are resolved as scripts (`_script_literals` walks for `ast.Constant` str ending in `.sh`). A script path built dynamically (f-string, `str(tmp_path / 'purge.sh')`, a fixture-returned Path, or a variable) is never resolved, so the destructive script is never scanned and the gate silently passes.
scenarios: A future test does `from subprocess import run` then `run(['sh','purge.sh'])` executing an unguarded destructive script
